content: Is there an easy way to elide uninteresting parts of a Lean definition in Verso? I see there's a bunch of code implemented for doing that in Theorem Proving in Lean (via anchors), but I don't see how to do it without copying a bunch of that code.

Not so much right now, but we can upstream some of that. Slides have a version of it too.

Would something that takes "magic comments" around the text to be elided, replacing it with "..." do the trick for you? Or do you need something a bit more configurable, with e.g. custom replacement text or styled replacement text?
Generally speaking, I try to wait for there to be two users of something before upstreaming it into Verso, just so we don't commit too early to something that's too hyper-specific for one user.

Yes, I think that'd fit my use-case.

But also after a day of playing around, I'm wondering if I need a whole new genre (at which point, I could just implement the magic comments myself) or if Verso just isn't the right tool for what I'm doing. The short version is that I'm trying to use Verso to replace lightweight code documentation like Markdown, but with Lean code and proofs attached. Right now I have something sort of working with Manual, where I'm manually hiding the ToC, search bar, etc. and manually merging the output files into a single page, but it's all kind of brittle. I thought for something this simple maybe I wanted no genre, but that seems to lose the Lean rendering functionality, which is also important.

Do you have any advice here? I'd be happy to share more of my imagined use-case in a separate chat if you're interested.
Maybe a quick call would be fastest?
